articles.title: Linear energy transfer optimization in proton therapy of sinonasal cancer
articles.summary: This research demonstrates that LET optimization in proton therapy can effectively reduce doses to critical organs at risk without compromising target coverage. The study emphasizes that the effectiveness of these optimizations is patient-specific and necessitates individualized assessment.

articles.title: An EPID-based virtual audit framework for multi-institutional radiotherapy audits using direct fluence comparison
articles.summary: This study proposes a tiered framework using EPID-based fluence comparisons to standardize radiotherapy machine parameters across institutions. The method shows promise in identifying cases that require review during multi-institutional quality assurance audits.

articles.title: Feasibility of organic thin-film transistors for real-time in vivo dosimetry
articles.summary: Researchers investigated the use of organic thin-film transistors for real-time dosimetry. The study found that these devices exhibit promising dosimetric characteristics in phantom studies, potentially offering a new tool for clinical in vivo monitoring.

articles.title: Implementation of a 0.55T MR simulator for intracranial stereotactic radiosurgery
articles.summary: This study evaluates the clinical feasibility of a low-field 0.55T MRI scanner for use as a dedicated radiotherapy simulator for intracranial stereotactic radiosurgery. The findings suggest it can meet imaging requirements for SRS planning, though further comparisons with high-field systems are needed.

articles.title: Sensitivity of silicon-to-water dose conversion and Bragg-peak metrics to stopping-power datasets in proton dosimetry
articles.summary: This study quantifies how water-to-silicon stopping-power ratios, converted dose-to-water distributions, and Bragg-peak metrics vary with the stopping-power dataset for a 67.5 MeV pristine proton beam in water. Accurate proton dosimetry requires internally consistent data for detector-to-water conversion and Monte Carlo simulations.

articles.title: In silico feasibility and robustness evaluation of a single-spot proton Bragg peak FLASH platform for small-animal irradiation using a generalized 3D-printed bolus
articles.summary: This research aims to develop an irradiation setup for ultra-high dose-rate Bragg peak proton delivery, moving beyond traditional transmission beams. The study evaluates a 3D-printed bolus approach to achieve more conformal clinical dose distributions in preclinical FLASH models.

articles.title: A comprehensive microdosimetric study of neutron capture enhanced proton therapy: physical dose to RBE-based evaluation
articles.summary: This Monte Carlo investigation assesses the physical dose deposition and microdosimetric characteristics of Neutron Capture Enhanced Proton Therapy (NCEPT). The study seeks to clarify conflicting reports regarding the effectiveness of NCEPT in clinical proton therapy.

articles.title: Evaluation of the efficacy and safety of particle therapy for kidney cancer through a multicenter registry study and meta-analysis
articles.summary: This multicenter study compares the outcomes of particle therapy, including proton beam therapy and carbon-ion radiotherapy, with stereotactic body radiation therapy for kidney cancer. The analysis provides clinical evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of particle therapy in this patient population.

articles.title: Continual learning in oncology AI: A framework for safe clinical translation
articles.summary: This review explores continual learning (CL) methods for AI models in oncology to address performance erosion caused by evolving imaging protocols, staging criteria, and therapies. The framework discusses maintaining model accuracy and patient safety through dynamic learning, with significant relevance to radiation oncology and medical imaging.

articles.title: Proton beam therapy in the treatment of adenoid cystic carcinoma of the head and neck: a single enterprise retrospective cohort study
articles.summary: This retrospective study evaluates the clinical outcomes of curative-intent proton beam therapy for adenoid cystic carcinoma of the head and neck. Findings suggest favorable local control and manageable toxicity, though the authors emphasize the need for larger studies to compare definitive versus postoperative approaches.

articles.title: RadCalc 3D Monte-Carlo: tuning and independent dosimetric validation of radiotherapy treatment plans
articles.summary: This study details the implementation and validation of an independent Monte-Carlo based dose recalculation software for patient-specific quality assurance. The research provides a framework for integrating high-accuracy dose calculation verification into clinical linear accelerator workflows.

articles.title: A depth-resolved single-flask 3D clonogenic platform for continuous LET-dependent radiobiological assessment in carbon-ion therapy
articles.summary: This study introduces a novel 3D clonogenic assay platform designed to capture depth-dependent biological responses across carbon-ion beam paths. The platform facilitates high-density spatial sampling, supporting more accurate biophysical model validation compared to traditional point-wise assays.

articles.title: CY 2027 Medicare Final Rules and Impact on Proton Therapy
articles.summary: CMS finalized the CY 2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule and Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System rules, which take effect January 1, 2027. The changes include significant updates to hospital outpatient payment rates for proton therapy services due to 340B drug payment redistribution, resulting in a projected increase for most common proton treatment codes.

articles.title: BayCare Proton Center Treats First Patient on Mevion S250 FIT™ with Leo Cancer Care's Marie® Solution
articles.summary: The BayCare Proton Center has successfully initiated patient treatments using the Mevion S250 FIT proton therapy system integrated with Leo Cancer Care's Marie solution. This installation marks a new technological implementation in a clinical setting for advanced proton delivery.

articles.title: 50 million Americans live in counties without a radiation oncology clinic, study finds
articles.summary: A recent study highlights that 50 million Americans reside in counties lacking a radiation oncology clinic, underscoring significant geographic disparities in access to cancer care. The findings emphasize the ongoing challenges in providing equitable radiation treatment coverage across the United States.

articles.title: ASTRO updates guideline on shorter-course radiation therapy for localized prostate cancer
articles.summary: The American Society for Radiation Oncology (ASTRO) has released updated clinical guidelines regarding the use of shorter-course radiation therapy for patients with localized prostate cancer. These evidence-based updates aim to provide clinicians with standardized recommendations for treatment fractionation.

articles.title: IBA treats first patient in clinical trial of FLASH proton therapy for head and neck cancer
articles.summary: IBA has announced the treatment of the first patient in the C-FLASH-01 clinical trial, evaluating the safety and efficacy of ConformalFLASH proton therapy. This trial marks a significant milestone in testing ultra-high dose rate radiation delivery for head and neck cancer patients.

articles.title: Hampton University Proton Cancer Institute opens new wellness space
articles.summary: The Hampton University Proton Cancer Institute has inaugurated a new wellness facility dedicated to supporting patients and their caregivers. This regional development enhances the supportive care infrastructure at this key proton therapy center in the DMV area.
